title: 11.11 sales and Deepavali long weekend draw shoppers to stores; lower airfares emerge as an online draw - 联合早报
text:
11.11 sales and Deepavali long weekend draw shoppers to stores; lower airfares emerge as an online draw | Lianhe Zaobao 
 Singapore International China Business Opinion Lifestyle Entertainment Search Wu Jiayun Published / 12 Nov 2026 15:59 S M L XL 11.11 sales and Deepavali long weekend draw shoppers to stores; lower airfares emerge as an online draw
 AI-translated article with transliterated names. Read original Chinese article here. 
 Shoppers browse on Wednesday afternoon at OG's Albert Complex outlet, which offered S$11 deals for the 11.11 shopping festival. （Photo: Tay Yee Miing） With the Deepavali long weekend coinciding with the 11.11 shopping festival, many malls and retailers were prompted to run promotions to capture both online and offline sales. Some merchants have reported a 30% increase in sales compared to last year. 
 This year, more travel platforms are seeking a share of the 11.11 spending buzz; consequently, some consumers are opting to purchase discounted airfares and spending their money on “experiences” instead. 
 Originally a shopping festival for e-commerce platforms, 11.11 has in recent years also seen Singapore's shopping malls run promotions across multiple channels. This year's Deepavali long weekend has given footfall a further boost. 
 Responding to queries on Wednesday (11 November), Gain City marketing manager Yang Huiling said sales had already risen 30% compared to last year's 11.11 event. “With this promotion coinciding with the Deepavali long weekend, more customers had time to visit our stores and enjoy the offers. Showroom visits have increased significantly.” 
 When Lianhe Zaobao visited department store OG's Albert Complex outlet on Monday (9 November) and Wednesday afternoon, weekday crowds showed no signs of thinning, with some shoppers making a special trip for the 11.11 offers. 
 OG offered a storewide 20% discount on Tuesday (10 November) and Wednesday, and set up a section featuring S$11 deals. Retiree Guo, 70, came for the offers after seeing a newspaper advertisement. Another retiree, Chen, 61, who travelled from Tampines, said, “I still prefer the experience of choosing things in person to shopping online.” 
 A spokesperson for major appliance and furniture retailer Courts also said sales were higher than usual over the previous weekend, especially for smart televisions and kitchen appliances. “Consumers used the holiday to visit stores to replace ageing appliances and buy new furniture, boosting conversion rates for in-store shopping and online orders collected in stores.” 
 Hotels and airlines vie for customers with 11.11 deals 
 The hotel and travel industry has also stepped up its 11.11 promotions, with travel platforms Skyscanner and Booking.com launching offers for the Singapore market for the first time. A Skyscanner spokesperson said discounts of up to 10% were available on five routes from Singapore, including to popular destinations such as Seoul and Taipei. The Skyscanner app's “DROPS” feature also shows deals for flight from Singapore, with discounts of up to 40%. 
 After comparing different platforms, shopper Zhang Ying, 23, chose Trip.com to book a year-end flight to Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam. She saved S$60 and also snapped up a hotel booking voucher. 
 She also booked discounted flights to Europe at the end of last month for next year. Her spending during the sales season has focused on travel, with less going towards retail purchases than in previous years. “I don't need to stock up on anything now, and online shopping platforms have offers from time to time anyway. I'd rather use the money to plan trips in advance.” 
 Longer sales campaigns prompt consumers to shop earlier 
 As competition intensifies, e-commerce platforms are extending their major sales campaigns, prompting consumers to start shopping earlier. Regina Lim, head of Group Card Payments & Personal Loans, OCBC , said card transaction volumes on major e-commerce platforms had risen by 15% to 20% in the run-up to 11.11. Fast-moving consumer goods, fashion and electronics were the leading spending categories. 
 Lim said, “We are seeing signs that customers are starting their 11.11 shopping earlier, rather than concentrating their purchases solely on the campaign day.” 
 Social media strategist Huang Hanwei, 36, who enjoys buying photography equipment, began tracking offers across platforms in late October. He eventually placed four orders on Shopee and bought a camera flash on Pinduoduo, spending about S$752 in total — more than in previous years. 
 He found the offers on Shopee, Pinduoduo and TikTok Shop the most attractive. “On major sale days, retailers and platforms make a particular effort to compete for traffic and sales... I'll add items I want but don't urgently need to my cart, then watch the prices before ordering.” 
 Singapore is increasingly becoming an important market for e-commerce platforms expanding overseas. Pinduoduo lowered the threshold for free delivery by offering “ free shipping on a single item ”, while Taobao subsequently announced it would invest 100 million yuan (S$19.22 million) in a range of promotions in Singapore. 
 Logistics worker Chen Jianliang, 32, previously used Taobao but switched to Pinduoduo for everyday essentials after it began offering free shipping on single items. He also shops on Shopee. Sales assistant Liao Yanzhen, 25, uses Pinduoduo to stock up on tissues and other daily necessities. “Delivery may be slower, but it's cheaper and shipping is free.”
